description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in chains and clusters.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a sample, likely from a culture of an aspirate. The field contains numerous gram-positive cocci, which appear as purple, round structures. These cocci are arranged in chains and clusters, suggesting a mixed morphology. The background is clear, and the staining technique highlights the bacterial cell walls.
visible_findings: purple staining of bacterial cell walls

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive rods in a clinical specimen.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a clinical specimen. Numerous purple-staining, rod-shaped bacteria are visible, consistent with gram-positive rods. The rods are arranged singly, in pairs, and in short chains. The background is clear, indicating a clean preparation. The staining technique highlights the bacterial morphology and gram-positive cell wall characteristics.
visible_findings: bacteria arranged singly, in pairs, and short chains

description.short_caption: Sagittal MRI of the lumbar spine showing abnormal findings.
description.detailed_description: This sagittal MRI image of the lumbar spine demonstrates the vertebral column, intervertebral discs, and spinal canal. There is evidence of abnormal signal intensity within the spinal canal, possibly indicating a pathological process such as infection, inflammation, or mass effect. The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) signal appears altered in certain areas, and there may be associated soft tissue changes. The image is de-identified and shows no patient-identifiable information.
visible_findings: sagittal view of the lumbar spine
altered signal intensity in the spinal canal
vertebral column and intervertebral discs visible
